messages.subject: Mentor's summit
messages.body_plain:
Until today I had not realized that the Mentor's summit was funded. I'm officially
retired, and my time is spent mostly on community work (see some of the CRAN optimization
stuff -- several packages and parts this year). I am willing to attend the Mentor's Summit
as one of the R group, but am fairly new to this game, so if there are two others eager,
I'll step back so there doesn't have to be a vote or such.

 From Carol Smith's emails, I'd guess we have to make up our minds in the next few days.

Cheers,

John Nash

messages.subject: Re: Mentor's summit
messages.body_plain:
To follow-up on John's post re the mentor summit:

i)   It's an 'unconference' as pioneered by the of the O'Reilly Events. It's
     semi-structured.

ii)  It's a decent way to meet some other folks from other open source projects.

iii) It's always late in October and always at Google HQ which throws in a
     spanner for those teaching in Europe.

iv)  The crowd is a tad younger on average than John but he would not be the
     only gray beard there.

v)   I've gone twice; I may go again but I am happy to take a backseat if two
     other folks want to go.  I sort-of have an invite from someone at Google
     to also talk RProtoBuf / Rcpp once there so it may make sense to go.

vi)  I guess we have five potential candidates for the two slots in the five
     mentors Roger, Stefan, John, Hadley and myself.  Stefan just took
     himself out of contention, John has raised his had, I hereby do so
     tentatively.   Roger, Hadley: please ping back.

vii) Admining is an issue. I am waiting on past year's info from Manuel/Fritz
     but should get that sorted out.

Cheers, Dirk

--
Dirk Eddelbuettel | e...@debian.org | http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com

messages.subject: Wrapping up GSoC/R 2010 write-up
messages.body_plain:
Dear GSoC students and mentors,

We should report the final status to the R community, GSoC and the world at
large. So at long last and a little belatedly, I just sat down and wrote up a
page based on the form used by Fritz and Manuel in 2008 and 2009.  Please see

     http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/tmp-r/soc10.html

Please read the draft page, and in particular 'your' paragraphs. This is
old-school html, so just use 'view source' and send me diffs or new paragraphs
when something is amiss.  I am sure I have misspelled a thing or two and
won't vouch for grammar or correctness either.

I would like to post this early next week. So if you have a chance to review
this over the weekend or on Monday, I would greatly appreciate it.

Thanks also to the three our of four who have uploaded to the Google Code
site.  If you haven't you know who you are and what we expect from you :)

Comments, criticism, corrections -- keep'em coming.

Cheers, Dirk

--
Dirk Eddelbuettel | e...@debian.org | http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com

THanks for putting this together. Only change suggested is from 'rdx' to 'radx'. I'm a bit
sensitive to the name Chillu originally chose: my mother was <100m from 880kg of rdx when
it went off in August 1944 and, we believe, died young in part due to injuries sustained.
I suspect there may be other people who have bad associations with the rdx name as well.

On other matters, has Google provided a PO yet for us? I don't need to claim until after,
but it would be good to know things are in place. I presume they want receipts etc., which
I"m used to providing.

Best,

JN

messages.subject: symbolic regression
messages.body_plain:
I've been going over the emails concerning the objections to symbolic
regression, and I have three questions:

1. Do you think it is possible to construct a symbolic regression
proposal which would be appropriate for R?

It seems unlikely to me that the idea of symbolic regression can't be
rescued by measuring goodness of fit carefully, and that doing so is a
worthy endeavor to advance statistics in its own right. 2. Is there
any evidence to the contrary?

3. Why is http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2010:syrfr
displaying in raw, unformatted wikitext?

Regards,
James Salsman

messages.subject: Re: symbolic regression
messages.body_plain:
Though I was instigator and mentor for radx project, my main interest in automatic vs
symbolic differentiation and other such tasks is to be able to generate gradients or
Jacobians when the function is not totally algebraic e.g., has IF() or other constructs. I
don't know enough yet to comment on feasibility. Nor can I comment on the wiki issue.

For me there is no objection to symbolic math tools for R. Quite the contrary.

One concern that affects all packages is that they should "work together" so that where
either will do the task, the user only needs a single calling style, with some sort of
parameter "method = 'symbolic'" etc. I'd be unhappy if there were great differences.
Indeed, in building optimx, Ravi and I had to leave out one or two methods because the
calling sequences were just too awkward. This is a general issue, but one that I believe
is very important to users, and I know from experience takes work and cooperation from
developers.

Best,

John Nash

messages.subject: The gsoc-r blog was added to R-bloggers
messages.subject_clean: The gsoc-r blog was added to R-bloggers
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
Congratulations to your success in this year's gsoc R projects.

After consulting with Dirk Eddelbuettel on the topic, I have added this year's gsoc R blog:
http://gsoc2010r.wordpress.com/
To R-bloggers:
http://www.r-bloggers.com/

This means that your online content from this summer will get (a bit) more exposure.  And that if any of you will have a follow-up to your project that you would like to post on the blog, then the content will now be visible to (approximately) 2,500 readers from the R community.

If any of you feels that you would rather have your content withdrawn (either from the blog, or from R-bloggers), for what ever reason, simply e-mail me and I'll remove it.

I wish you all many more successful projects,
Best,
Tal
